text: 📸 Jornada Nacional por la Paz — Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas, 6 de noviembre de 2026

🇲🇽✊ "It is very machista that women have to hide our age. Women can be whatever we want to be, and we age with dignity, just like men." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ocozocoautla, Chiapas "This year I turned 64," she told the students in Ocozocoautla, recalling that she grew up in a time when women were told never to say their age, "as if growing old were something bad." She then told them how she studied at the UNAM's CCH Sur high school, studied physics, then did a master's and a doctorate in engineering, including time abroad: "I could not have done that if the UNAM had not given me a scholarship to study."

🇲🇽✊ "Make the most of this scholarship, because it is not the president who gives it to you. Do you know who gives it? The people of Mexico. The people of Mexico, who pay their taxes, give back to the students of Chiapas a scholarship." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ocozocoautla, Chiapas National scholarships coordinator Julio César León said the well-being scholarship system now covers 19.5 million students nationwide and expects to reach 22 million this year. Chiapas is one of only five states where the Gertrudis Bocanegra scholarship extends coverage to 100% of students, from primary through university. "What we want to achieve is the right to education, that it never be interpreted as a privilege, but as a right." Sheinbaum: the scholarship is "not only to fulfill a personal dream, but to keep fulfilling the dream of all Mexicans: a Mexico always free, independent."

🇲🇽🎨 "Now, as the first woman president, it falls to me, and to all women and all men, to recognize the great heroines of our homeland." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Ocozocoautla, Chiapas Handing out the new Gertrudis Bocanegra university scholarship on November 6, she asked how many heroines students learned about in school: "At most Josefa Ortiz de Domínguez," and Margarita Maza only as Benito Juárez's wife, "but not what Margarita Maza did." Gertrudis Bocanegra, a woman of good social position in Michoacán, gave her resources to the independence cause, like Leona Vicario. The viceroyalty's army arrested her and demanded the names of the independence fighters. She gave none, and was executed in the plaza of Pátzcuaro. "Mexico is full of heroes and heroines who gave us what we are today."

🇲🇽🎨 "Chiapas is the only state of the Republic that voted on whether they wanted to be Mexican. And in 1824 they said: 'We want to be Mexican.'" — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas After independence, Chiapas, part of the colonial Captaincy General of Guatemala, joined Mexico by popular consultation, proclaimed on September 14, 1824. Governor Eduardo Ramírez recalled that Chiapa de Corzo is named for General Ángel Albino Corzo, who fought beside Benito Juárez for the Reform, and that the Chiapa people threw themselves from the Sumidero Canyon rather than submit to the Spanish conquerors. Sheinbaum added that Chiapas is one of the few states where every young person who goes on to a public university keeps a scholarship. 31 new Margarita Maza high schools are being built in the state.

🇲🇽🎨 "If the boyfriend tells the girlfriend, 'Hey, don't wear such a short skirt,' that is not okay, because it is up to her how she wants to wear her skirt. Nobody should be told how to dress. Love is recognizing people as they are." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas The ABC of Emotions guides cover changes in the body, responsible use of social media, love and relationships, and violence, including "attitudes we sometimes take that don't look like violence, but are," like a partner demanding to see your phone: "The person has to decide whether they want to show the other what is on their phone." She said talking openly about it in class helps keep young people away from drugs and alcohol, and gave students the Línea de la Vida helpline, 800 911 2000, for anyone facing a bigger problem.
banner: "LOVE IS RECOGNIZING PEOPLE AS THEY ARE"

text: 🇲🇽🎨 "On social media there are stereotypes. And the beauty stereotype turns out to be a woman who is not Mexican, or a man who is not Mexican. Is that beauty? No. It is a stereotype that they make us believe is beauty." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Chiapa de Corzo, Chiapas On November 6 at CONALEP 22 in Chiapa de Corzo, Sheinbaum launched the National Day for Peace and the "ABC of Emotions": three guides, for students, for parents and for teachers, written with input from young people, to be discussed in class on Mondays in the last year of secondary school and in all high schools. She added that many video games reward violence: "if you kill more, then you are better than others." Education Secretary Mario Delgado said the students there estimated they spend about 4 hours a day on their phones, a little more than one full day a week.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>AMETEK Picks Tamaulipas: $25 Million, 650 New Jobs</u>

US precision manufacturer AMETEK will expand in Reynosa and Nuevo Laredo after weighing other states, El Economista reports: a combined $25 million investment and 650 jobs, 400 in Reynosa and 250 in Nuevo Laredo. The company already employs 2,600 people in Reynosa, serving medical, aerospace and semiconductor industries.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>2027 Ballot Approved: PRD Out, PAZ and SOMOS In</u>

The INE's General Council approved the ballot for the June 6, 2027 federal deputies election. It carries eight emblems: PAN, PRI, PVEM, PT, MC, Morena and newcomers PAZ and SOMOS. The PRD's logo is gone after the party lost its registration in 2024. More than 100 million ballots will be printed.

🇲🇽⚖️ <u>INE Sets a Nine-Point Transparency Plan for 2026-2027</u>

With its supplier contracts under federal investigation, Mexico's electoral institute approved a nine-point work program on transparency and personal data, with deliverables, responsible units and deadlines for each action. Councillor Jorge Montaño Ventura: "It is not enough to issue a resolution. What matters is that it is carried out and that citizens can understand it."
